assumptions_and_boundaries.name: Vec::last_mut through slice DerefMut
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: Rust 1.96 first borrows the last mutable element with `self.last_mut()?`. The harness models only the empty-Vec None case and the non-empty relation between the original Vec prefix, borrowed last element, and final Vec view after the predicate mutates that borrowed element.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: FnOnce(&mut T) predicate observation on the last element
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The target body calls the user predicate exactly once on the borrowed last element. The harness records only the observed boolean and final value of that borrowed element; it does not strengthen the predicate relation or assume the target postcondition.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: Vec::pop tail removal after true predicate
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: Rust 1.96 calls `self.pop()` only on the true predicate branch. The harness models only the source-backed empty/non-empty pop effects needed after the last-element predicate observation and does not mark alloc::vec::Vec::pop complete.

notes: The public target method is executable and non-external-body: the harness keeps the Rust 1.96 flow `let last = self.last_mut()?; if predicate(last) { self.pop() } else { None }`, adapted only to an explicit match and a named FnOnce observation boundary.
